title: The voice that is not allowed to make anything up
angle: Agentic depth, latency, multimodal. Four server tools are the agent's only route to a fact, and a fifth turns the page while it is still speaking. Built — one key away.
endline: He gets the page. He stays liable, and he stays right.

marks.do: The workshop. The bike on the lift, the phone face down.
Open the KTM. Tap VOICE. "Nothing is loaded until I press that button."
"How much engine oil does it take?" — watch the page turn mid-sentence.
"Walk me through changing the oil filter." It is reading the book out loud.
"What's the valve clearance?" — the refusal. THE moment.
Hold a chain to the camera. Contextual update, not an answer.
"Und wie viel Öl?" — its own words translate, the manual's do not.
Latency: theirs published, ours measured. Say which is which.
One policy, two engines — the test that fails if they drift.

slides.kicker: Honesty up front — say it in one sentence and move on
slides.text: The voice mode that is live today runs on Deepgram. The ElevenLabs path is a real second engine, and it needs one API key and nothing else.
slides.sub: Everything in it is code in the repo with *29 passing tests* and a `--dry-run` that prints every request body. Nothing in it has touched a live ElevenLabs account, because there is no key on this machine. *A judge who finds that themselves has stopped listening to the rest.*
notes: Say it once, on camera, in the first thirty seconds. Then never mention it again.
If the key does not exist on the day, run the same demo on Deepgram and say ~same policy, same tools, one key away~. Never mime a session that did not happen.
Do not imply any of §2 has run. elevenlabs/chat-ui.patch is *not applied*.

defs.d: api/tests/test_voice_elevenlabs.py, ElevenLabs HTTP mocked. 617 passed / 20 skipped across api/tests.

slides.text: The agent has no vocabulary of its own. Four server tools are the only things it is allowed to say.
slides.sub: `find_procedure` · `read_page` · `get_spec` · `list_parts` — each returns the manual's own printed words with the page they are printed on. Temperature 0. It must call one before the first word of any answer. *The deepest thing a voice agent can do in this product is the thing it is forbidden from doing everywhere else: it may not answer.*
notes: "That constraint is the demo." Say it exactly that way.

A fifth tool, show_page, is a client tool with execution_mode: immediate — the page appears *during* the sentence that names it, not after the turn ends. One field, and it is the difference between a voice assistant and a pair of hands.

The manual id is bound by a substituted header, not by a model argument, so the agent cannot be talked into reading a different book. Five tests cover it, including "the model asks for the BMW, the header says KTM, the header wins."

slides.title: Everything orange is theirs. Every arrow into the model comes out of a PDF.
slides.caption: Server tools are called by ElevenLabs, not by the tab. The one client tool turns the page.
notes: Read it once, out loud, as: ~everything black is ElevenLabs, everything cream is ours, and every arrow into the model comes out of a PDF.~ Then stop.

Deepgram is stateless — we push the whole prompt, models and tool endpoints down the socket every session. An ElevenLabs agent is a persistent workspace object with one static prompt and tool ids, and the per-session facts arrive as dynamic variables. That is why there is a separate setup tool, session endpoint, credential flow and manual-id binding.
Why WebRTC and not the WebSocket: a WebSocket is TCP, so one lost packet head-of-line blocks the audio behind it. WebRTC drops a frame instead of stalling a sentence.

slides.text: This manual doesn't print a valve clearance.
slides.cite: the agent, asked for a figure the KTM manual does not carry
notes: *That is the whole product in one sentence. Every other assistant would have given me a number.*

One deliberate exception, narrowly scoped: when a function result shows the manual naming the job but printing no steps, the agent says "the manual doesn't print the steps" in four words, then gives the ordinary workshop procedure marked as general. *That licence covers steps and order only. It never covers a number.*
The same four tools already serve the typed chat path, which is evaluated: 100% of 43 quotes verbatim, 0 invented numbers, 0 dealer referrals over 25 questions.

defs.d: chat quotes verbatim on the page they name — api/eval/chat-report.md (measured).
invented numbers · dealer referrals, of 25 answers (measured).

slides.kicker: Multimodal, and the most interesting decision in the integration
slides.text: Its own words translate. The manual's do not.
slides.sub: A German mechanic asks *"Wieviel Öl?"* and the agent answers in German. But the manual is printed in English, and *translating a printed figure is paraphrasing a figure.* So numbers, units, part designations and page numbers come out in the manual's own language, word for word. Everything around them is German.
notes: "That is a sentence no generic voice wrapper has ever had to write." Say it and let it land.

Multimodal in one session: voice, the page, and the camera. The mechanic holds a part up, our classifier labels it, and the labels enter as a *contextual update* — context, never an answer — so the agent must still look the part up in the book. Typed turns go into the same conversation.

Why not their knowledge base / RAG: a RAG answer is a paraphrase with a citation stapled on, and this mechanic is liable for the number. Also — 14,770 distinct free English PDFs. Uploading them into a knowledge base is a copy we have no right to make.

slides.kicker: One policy, two engines — enforced by a test
slides.text: The grounding policy isn't rewritten for this. It is imported from the other engine, and a test asserts the two prompts are identical character for character.
slides.sub: `prompt_template()` calls `voice._prompt()` — the Deepgram agent's own prompt function — with the per-manual facts replaced by dynamic variables. *Edit the policy in one place and both engines move together; fork it and CI fails.*
notes: This is the answer to "so this is a Deepgram app with an ElevenLabs sticker". The opposite: what is shared is the one thing that should be, and it is shared by import with a test that fails if they drift.
Close, back on the bike with the page open and the lines orange: ~He gets the page. He stays liable, and he stays right. That's the whole thing.~
Cost: not measurable for ElevenLabs yet — that is a key away too. The comparable voice engine bills $0.075 per connected minute of socket time, which exists only between two taps of one button.

items: ElevenLabs voice is never "live" — GET /api/voice/config returns elevenlabsAgentId: null.
The 3D backdrop is a technical grid. No panorama, no photographic workshop scene.
Dropbox folder sync and Climate Fit are "built, deploying", not deployed.
Never quote a running ledger total without the date beside it.
Never call 13,537 "manuals" — distinct fetchable PDFs is 14,770.
There is no checkout. "Live prices", never "buy".

notes: Presenter-only. The audience sees the end card.
Five steps to make it live are in elevenlabs.md §6: create the key, save it to agent-secrets/elevenlabs.txt, run tools/elevenlabs_setup.py, set ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID, deploy.
